issues: The spell effect is encoded as noop but should implement 'Select an enemy follower on the field. It cannot deal damage this turn.' No implemented ability in the reference represents a temporary 'can't deal damage' debuff on a targeted follower; add an operation such as a targeted temporary damage-prevention/attack-suppression effect, then replace noop with that effect.

The activated ability target selector incorrectly puts a DeckFilter under targets.filter for a selfFollower target. It should select a Fable follower on your field, but target filtering by trait is not supported in the listed TargetSelector schema. Add support for trait/card filters on field target selectors (or a dedicated target selector for ally followers by trait), then encode the addCounter target using that instead of the current invalid targets.filter structure.

The fanfare ability target selector incorrectly uses targets.filter with selfFollower to represent 'Select a Pixie follower on your field.' Target filtering by name is not supported in the listed TargetSelector schema. Add support for identity/card filters on field target selectors (or a dedicated named follower selector), then encode the buff target as a Pixie follower instead of the current invalid targets.filter structure.

The activated ability returns this amulet to hand, but returnToHand targets only cover field followers/enemy followers in examples and 'self' is defined as this card/this follower. Add explicit engine support for returning the source card itself (including amulets) to hand, then encode the activated effect as return this card to hand rather than relying on self ambiguously.

The cemetery condition is encoded as spellchain 6, but the source requires 'at least 6 cards with different base costs in your cemetery,' not spells with different names. It should use a condition for distinct base costs in your cemetery; add such a condition to the engine and replace spellchain with it.

The fanfare is encoded as noop but should implement 'You may put a follower from your hand onto your field.' No implemented operation supports putting a chosen follower from hand onto the field, so add an effect such as selectFromHand/to field or summonFromHand, then encode that optional summon.

The summoned follower should have 'Its fanfare abilities can't be performed.' No implemented operation suppresses a card's fanfare on entering from hand this way; add an effect or summon flag to disable fanfare resolution for the chosen follower, then encode it.

The summoned follower should also have 'For the rest of this turn, it can't attack enemies.' No implemented operation grants a temporary attack restriction against enemy targets to a selected follower; add a temporary attack-restriction effect, then encode it on the chosen follower instead of noop.

The onEvolve ability is encoded as noop but should implement 'You may put any number of followers from your hand onto your field.' No implemented operation supports selecting any number of followers from hand and putting them onto the field, so add an effect such as multi-select from hand to field, then encode that optional summon.

The followers put onto the field should have 'Their fanfare abilities can't be performed.' No implemented operation suppresses fanfare for multiple followers entering this way; add an effect or summon flag to disable fanfare resolution for those followers, then encode it.

The followers put onto the field should also have 'For the rest of this turn, they can't attack enemies.' No implemented operation grants this temporary attack restriction to multiple summoned followers; add a temporary attack-restriction effect for chosen/summoned followers, then encode it instead of noop.

The conditional extra damage to leaders is encoded as dealDamageAllEnemies with followersOnly false, which would also damage enemy followers again. The source says 'deal 2 damage to each enemy leader' only. No implemented operation deals damage to all enemy leaders without affecting followers; add an operation for damaging each enemy leader, then replace the second step with that effect.
